newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga hails agreement signed by Sri Lanka's two key political parties last week to work together to end the ethnic conflict as an opportunity to forget narrow political differences.
Average Sri Lankan family today spends 70 percent of income on food, a government agricultural institute says.
Doctors to go on four-day strike next week if government fails to meet their demands for salary rivisions, the powerful Government Medical Officers' Association says.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels capture navy boat with eight servicemen on board off the coast of northwestern Mannar on Thursday.

Government launches programme to rebuild northern Jaffna library, considered a storehouse of Tamil literature and allegedly burnt down by police in 1981, as a reconciliatory move towards the people of the town.
Sri Lankans celebrate Sinhalese and Tamil New Year on Sunday and Monday. Offices, banks and liquor shops closed during this time.
Police arrest three suspected LTTE activists from lodging house at Colombo's busy Maradana locality.
